new_construction_exemption.basis: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from limits on periodic increases for the initial mortgage amortization period or 30 years after completion of construction (issuance of the Certificate of Occupancy), whichever is shorter. The exemption is 30 years if there is no initial mortgage financing. The landlord must apply to the Rent Control Board for certification.

unverifiable_exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings certified as exempt by the Rent Control Board (up to 30 years)
Dwellings vacant for at least 18 months, exempt for 5 years after a Board-determined substantial rehabilitation
Units rehabilitated under federal or state Rental Rehabilitation Programs that receive Section 8 subsidies or federal vouchers
Units under a landlord contract with a governmental agency that regulates the rent
coverage.summary: All multiple dwellings (any building with one or more apartments rented or offered for rent) are subject to rent control. Exempt: public housing, hotel or motel space rented day to day to transients, commercial space, newly constructed multiple dwellings (up to 30 years), substantially rehabilitated vacant dwellings (5 years), certain Section 8 rehabilitation units, and units under a governmental agency rent-regulation contract.
coverage.owner_conditions: The chapter defines 'owner occupied' (four units or fewer, with the owner living in one), but does not list owner-occupied dwellings as exempt. The definition is used only for the inspection-fee waiver.

evidence.quoted_span: All multiple dwellings, as defined in subsection 19:2-2, are subject to Rent Control pursuant to this Title XIX Rent Control,
Shall mean and include any building or structure and land appurtenant thereto containing one or more apartments or rented or offered for rent to one or more tenants or family units.
Any motel or hotel space rented on a day-to-day basis to transients;
Any dwelling, building or structure, or portion thereof, rented for commercial use;
All multiple dwellings, as defined in subsection 19:2-2, are subject to Rent Control pursuant to this Title XIX Rent Control,

The provisions of the Rent Control Ordinance, which limit the periodic or regular increases in base rentals of dwelling units shall not apply to newly constructed multiple dwellings for a period of time not to exceed the period of amortization of any initial mortgage loan obtained for the multiple dwelling, or for 30 years following completion of construction, whichever is less.
In the event that there is no initial mortgage financing, the period of the exemption from rent control shall be 30 years from the completion of the construction.

the landlord of any newly constructed dwelling shall apply to the Rent Control Board for a Certification that the dwelling, or portion thereof with respect to Temporary Certificates of Occupancy, is granted an exemption from any restrictions in the rent that the landlord may charge.
Shall mean the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy pursuant to the "State Uniform Construction Code Act" P.L. 1975. c. 217 (N.J.S.A. 52:27D-133)
Shall mean any dwelling of four units or less in at least one unit of which the owner resides.
There is no inspection fee for owner-occupied units.
Newly constructed multiple dwellings and vacant dwellings as set forth in this chapter at Subsections 19:2-18.1 and 19:2-18.2, respectively;

Dwellings which become vacant and remain vacant for a minimum of 18 months or dwellings which are already vacant on the effective date of this section shall be exempt for a period of five years from any restrictions in the rent that the landlord may charge, if the Rent Control Board determines that the cost of reconstruction or rehabilitation during a twelve-month period has exceeded 50% of the fair market value of the dwelling

Those units which have been rehabilitated by the Federal and State Rental Rehabilitation Programs as administered by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, the New Jersey Department of Community Affairs or the New Jersey Housing Mortgage Finance Agency and will be receiving Section 8 rent subsidies or Federal housing vouchers.
A contract between a landlord and a governmental agency duly providing for that governmental agency to regulate the amount of rent received by that landlord

result.notes: I set other_conditions to null. It described landlord conduct (annual registration and substantial compliance before an increase), which is a precondition for raising rent, not a coverage fact about buildings, units or owners. The vacant-dwelling exemption now states that the dwelling must have been vacant for at least 18 months (§ 19:2-18.2a). requires_unknown_facts stays false: the chapter covers all multiple dwellings, and the subsidy, contract, new-construction and rehabilitation exemptions are listed as unverifiable exemptions. I left construction_cutoff null because the new-construction exemption is a rolling 30-year window that the landlord must apply for, not a fixed date. min_units stays null: the definition reaches buildings with one or more apartments, so there is no meaningful minimum.
